title: Implications of Recent Agreement with Malaysia to Suspend Overlapping Claims in Singapore's Territorial Waters off Tuas
what_it_is: Implications of Recent Agreement with Malaysia to Suspend Overlapping Claims in Singapore's Territorial Waters off Tuas

sections.label: Malaysian vessels in Singapore waters
sections.summary: Malaysian government vessels anchored illegally since December 2018 must move out, with negotiations to follow if recommendations are implemented by 14 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Malaysian government vessels which have been illegally anchored in our waters since early December 2018 would have to move out.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In keeping with past practice, no commercial activities or anchoring of ships would be allowed in this area.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our ships will continue to patrol and take appropriate enforcement actions within our territorial waters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: If all these recommendations are implemented by 14 April 2019, then negotiations for maritime boundary delimitation in the area will start within one month thereafter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I need to stress that these measures shall be taken without prejudice to the respective maritime boundary claims of both sides.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This will allow the ground situation to be de-escalated, and then both sides can embark on maritime boundary delimitation negotiations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This is a process that will take time, but both sides are committed to negotiate in good faith, and in the event that we are unable to arrive at an amicable solution on delimitation, we may mutually agree to resort to an appropriate international third-party dispute settlement procedure on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, are there no more foreign ships right now in our territorial waters off Tuas at this point of time?

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: There are two Malaysian government vessels which I believe are still anchored there at this point in time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, the terms of the agreement have not been implemented yet.
